annotation.title_clean: Ethical considerations in the era of AI, automation, and surgical robots: there are plenty of lessons from the past
annotation.title_en: Ethical considerations in the era of AI, automation, and surgical robots: there are plenty of lessons from the past
annotation.summary_en: Perspective article drawing on the history of the da Vinci surgical robot to argue for ethical, liability and regulatory frameworks before surgical automation arrives. It uses biomedical ethics principles, proposes adapting SAE J3016 autonomy levels to surgical robots, and warns that manufacturers must not evade responsibility.
key_provisions_or_claims: Early surgical robot adoption caused harm through inadequate training and inflated marketing claims, undermining patient autonomy and non-maleficence.
Robust regulations, frameworks and standards for automated surgical systems are lacking.
SAE J3016 driving automation levels could be adapted as a framework for surgical robot autonomy.
Responsibility and liability for errors in autonomous surgery need early clarification; manufacturers must not shirk responsibility.
Military funding of surgical robotics raises concerns about differing ethical and legal standards.
